statement: Related work Zhang et al. give a completeness result for KAT together with axiom (T), in terms of guarded string languages [33, Theorem 9]. They observe that this axiomatisation is incomplete for REL, that it does not suffice to properly express incorrectness triples, and they leave the existence of a complete axiomatisation for relational models open. Our Theorem 4.16 gives a positive answer to this question, in the more primitive setting of plain Kleene algebra, without tests. We believe that a similar answer holds also for KAT; if this is the case, then we would obtain a system where we can reason purely equationally about incorrectness triples, as envisioned by Zhang et al.
context: 1 considering subalgebras where only certain relations are kept, since otherwise the only greatest relation is the full one. 2 Such a technique is somehow implicit in Kozen and Smith’s completeness proof for KAT [20] and Ésik et al.’s completeness proof for Kleene algebra with converse [4, 13]. Related work Zhang et al. give a completeness result for KAT together with axiom (T), in terms of guarded string languages [33, Theorem 9]. They observe that this axiomatisation is incomplete for REL, that it does not suffice to properly express incorrectness triples, and they leave the existence of a complete axiomatisation for relational models open. Our Theorem 4.16 gives a positive answer to this question, in the more primitive setting of plain Kleene algebra, without tests. We believe that a similar answer holds also for KAT; if this is the case, then we would obtain a system where we can reason purely equationally about incorrectness triples, as envisioned by Zhang et al. For the weaker theory of KAT with (T), the main completeness results of Zhang et al. [33, Theorems 7 and 9] are wrong: the model of guarded strings they designed equates too many expressions (namely, Σ∗ and ⊤ – see Remark 3.6). Our Theorem 3.5 uses a different language model, and we believe our simple (and linear) reduction from KA with (T) to KA is also a reduction from KAT with (T) to KAT, so that, e.g., [33, Theorem 10] about the complexity of KAT with (T) remains true.
